advances: The normalized parity-autocorrelation measure has an exact quadratic marginal-depth transfer.  In the registered \(n=2\) setting, the actual marginal \(W/4\)-depth of \(z_0\) produces a target-fiber profile \(\kappa_c\leq w_c\) of total mass \(W/4\) whose closed-halfspace depth at \(z_0\) is at least \(W/64\), with no dependence on \(d\).  If this single dominated profile can be realized along one affine fiber-depth graph, it is already an anchored affine certificate of value \(W/64\).  An exact abstract residual calibration shows both that the constant \(W/64\) is sharp for this autocorrelation argument and that deleting the diagonal destroys all marginal depth even when the global off-diagonal same-parity mass is far above the registered strict threshold.  Thus the remaining unsupported step is precisely affine realization of the dominated full-autocorrelation profile, not another scalar use of the strict global off-diagonal mass.

proof:
Compactness of \(C\) implies that only finitely many integer fibers have
positive volume.  Fix a closed halfspace \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and for
each \(r\in R_+\) put
\[
q_r:=\sum_{\substack{z\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^n\\z\equiv r\pmod2}}w_z.
\]
If two base points \(z,z'\) belong to \(Q\), then their midpoint belongs to
\(Q\) because \(Q\) is convex.  Therefore every pair of points in the
restrictions of \(\mu_r\) to base points in \(Q\) contributes to
\(K_r(Q\times\mathbb R^d)\), including pairs whose midpoint lies on the
closed boundary.  Hence
\[
K_r(Q\times\mathbb R^d)\geq\frac{q_r^2}{W_r}.
\tag{17}
\]
Summing (17) with the factor \(2^{-n}\) gives the first inequality in (1).
Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives
\[
\sum_{r\in R_+}\frac{q_r^2}{W_r}
\geq
\frac{\left(\sum_{r\in R_+}q_r\right)^2}
{\sum_{r\in R_+}W_r}
=\frac{w(Q)^2}{W},
\tag{18}
\]
which proves the second inequality in (1).  Empty parity classes do not
enter (17), and their corresponding \(q_r\) are zero.

Accepted fact `aca624dd8874e5a5` applies to the measure and normalization
used here.  It states that \(\mathsf A\mu\) has mass \(2^{-n}W\) and that
every target fiber has mass at most the original fiber volume.  This is
exactly (2), including zero-volume fibers.  When \(n=2\), equations (1) and
(3) give
\[
\kappa(Q)\geq
\frac14\frac{(W/4)^2}{W}
=\frac W{64},
\]
proving (4).

We verify the affine-lifting interface.  If \(z_0\notin P\), strong
separation from the compact polytope \(P\) gives a proper closed halfspace
of \(\mathbb R^2\) containing \(z_0\) and disjoint from \(P\).  Its
\(\kappa\)-mass is zero, contradicting (4).  Thus \(z_0\in P\).

Assume first that \(q>0\).  Every proper closed halfspace \(R\) of
\(\operatorname{aff}(P)\) containing \(z_0\) is the intersection with
\(\operatorname{aff}(P)\) of a proper closed halfspace \(Q\) of
\(\mathbb R^2\) containing \(z_0\): extend a nonconstant affine functional
defining \(R\) from \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\) to \(\mathbb R^2\).
Because \(\kappa\) is supported on \(P\), equations (4) and (5) give
\[
\sum_{c\in P\cap R\cap\mathbb Z^2}\delta_C(c,s(c))
\geq
\sum_{c\in P\cap R\cap\mathbb Z^2}\kappa_c
=\kappa(Q)
\geq\frac W{64}.
\]
Taking the infimum proves (6).  If \(q=0\), then \(P=\{z_0\}\);
\(\kappa_{z_0}=\sum_c\kappa_c=W/4\), and (5) gives (7), in fact with
\(W/4\) in place of \(W/64\).  Every vertex of the lattice polytope \(P\)
is a point of the support of \(\kappa\), and hence has positive original
fiber volume by (2).  Taking \(E=\operatorname{vert}(P)\) is therefore
admissible in the registered definition.  Its lattice hull is
\(P\cap\mathbb Z^2\), so (6) or (7) is exactly the claimed anchored
certificate.

It remains to verify the calibration.  There are twelve points
\(ku_j\) in (8), and each has mass \(1/16\).  Thus
\[
\varepsilon+\left(\frac14-\varepsilon\right)
+12\cdot\frac1{16}=1.
\]
Equations (9) are immediate from \(0<\varepsilon<1/64\).

The support lies on four distinct lines through the origin, in the
directions \(u_+,u_1,u_2,u_3\).  A line through the origin contains the
anchor and points from at most one of these four directional groups.  Its
mass is therefore at most
\[
\max\left\{
\varepsilon+\frac14-\varepsilon,\
\varepsilon+\frac14
\right\}
=\frac14+\varepsilon<\frac12.
\tag{19}
\]
A line not through the origin meets each of the four directional lines in
at most one point.  If it contains \(u_+\), its mass is at most
\[
\left(\frac14-\varepsilon\right)+3\cdot\frac1{16}
=\frac7{16}-\varepsilon<\frac12;
\]
if it does not, its mass is at most \(3/16\).  This proves (10) for every
affine lattice line, and hence for every primitive rank-one coset.

The three positive support points \(u_+,5u_1,5u_3\) are noncollinear and
satisfy
\[
10u_++5u_1+5u_3=0.
\]
All three coefficients are positive, so \(0\) lies in the interior of
their triangle.  This proves (11).

For a proper closed halfspace containing \(0\), moving its boundary to
\(0\) only makes it smaller.  A boundary-through-\(0\) halfspace is
\(\{x:\ell(x)\geq0\}\) for a nonzero linear functional \(\ell\).  Since
\[
2u_++u_1+u_3=0,
\]
the three numbers \(\ell(u_+),\ell(u_1),\ell(u_3)\) cannot all be negative.
The halfspace therefore contains the entire support group on at least one
of these three rays, as well as the anchor on its boundary.  The least
possible resulting mass is
\[
\left(\frac14-\varepsilon\right)+\varepsilon=\frac14.
\]
On the other hand, \(Q_+\) contains only \(0\) and \(u_+\) from the positive
support, so its mass is exactly \(1/4\).  This proves exact marginal depth
\(1/4\).

Every nonzero support point has parity \((1,0)\): the multipliers in
\(\mathcal K\) are odd, and each of \(u_+,u_1,u_2,u_3\) has odd first and
even second coordinate.  The anchor has parity \((0,0)\).  Consequently,
\[
W_{10}=1-\varepsilon,\qquad W_{00}=\varepsilon,
\]
and the other two parity masses vanish.  Direct calculation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q^\circ
&=(1-\varepsilon)^2+\varepsilon^2
-\left[
\left(\frac14-\varepsilon\right)^2+\varepsilon^2
+12\left(\frac1{16}\right)^2
\right]\\
&=\frac{57}{64}-\frac32\varepsilon.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(0<\varepsilon<1/64\), this is greater than \(111/128\), hence greater
than \(1/16\), while
\((16-e)/256<16/256=1/16\).  This proves (12).

Finally consider a distinct same-parity pair from the support.  The anchor
has no distinct partner of its parity.  In parity \((1,0)\), if neither
endpoint is \(u_+\), both first coordinates are at most \(-5\).  If one
endpoint is \(u_+\), the other has first coordinate at most \(-5\), so the
sum of their first coordinates is at most \(-4\).  The pair
\((u_+,u_+)\) is diagonal and is excluded from (13).  Thus every
off-diagonal same-parity midpoint has strictly negative first coordinate,
which proves (15).

For the full autocorrelation, the only pairs with midpoint in \(Q_+\) are
the two diagonal pairs at \(0\) and \(u_+\).  Using the normalization in
(1) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\kappa(Q_+)
&=\frac14\left[
\frac{\varepsilon^2}{\varepsilon}
+
\frac{(1/4-\varepsilon)^2}{1-\varepsilon}
\right]\\
&=\frac14\left[
\varepsilon+
\frac{(1/4-\varepsilon)^2}{1-\varepsilon}
\right]
=\frac1{64}+\frac{9\varepsilon}{64(1-\varepsilon)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves (16) and all assertions.
statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\) be a convex body, and write
\[
C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},\qquad
w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),\qquad
W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z>0.
\]
For \(r\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^n\), put
\[
W_r:=\sum_{z\equiv r\pmod 2}w_z,\qquad
R_+:=\{r:W_r>0\}.
\]
Let \(\mu_z\) be Lebesgue measure on \(\{z\}\times C_z\), let
\(\mu_r:=\sum_{z\equiv r\pmod2}\mu_z\), and put
\[
T(p,q):=\frac{p+q}{2},\qquad
K_r:=\frac1{W_r}T_\#(\mu_r\otimes\mu_r)\quad(r\in R_+),
\]
\[
\mathsf A\mu:=2^{-n}\sum_{r\in R_+}K_r,\qquad
\kappa_c:=(\mathsf A\mu)(\{c\}\times\mathbb R^d).
\]
For a closed halfspace \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), write
\[
w(Q):=\sum_{z\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^n}w_z,\qquad
\kappa(Q):=\sum_{c\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^n}\kappa_c.
\]
Then every closed halfspace \(Q\) satisfies the exact lower bound
\[
\kappa(Q)
\geq
2^{-n}\sum_{r\in R_+}
\frac{
\left(\sum_{\substack{z\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^n\\z\equiv r\pmod2}}w_z\right)^2
}{W_r}
\geq
2^{-n}\frac{w(Q)^2}{W}.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover, accepted fact `aca624dd8874e5a5` gives
\[
\sum_c\kappa_c=2^{-n}W,\qquad 0\leq\kappa_c\leq w_c
\quad(c\in\mathbb Z^n).
\tag{2}
\]

In particular, suppose \(n=2\) and \(z_0\in\mathbb Z^2\) satisfies
\[
w(Q)\geq\frac W4
\tag{3}
\]
for every proper closed halfspace \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) containing
\(z_0\).  Then
\[
\kappa(Q)\geq\frac W{64}
\tag{4}
\]
for every such \(Q\).

There is also the following exact affine-lifting interface.  Put
\[
P:=\operatorname{conv}\{c\in\mathbb Z^2:\kappa_c>0\},
\qquad q:=\dim\operatorname{aff}(P).
\]
Equation (4) implies \(z_0\in P\).  For \((c,x)\in C\), define
\[
\delta_C(c,x):=
\inf\left\{
\operatorname{vol}_d(C_c\cap J):
J\subseteq\mathbb R^d
\text{ is a proper closed halfspace and }x\in J
\right\}.
\]
Suppose there is an affine map
\[
s:\operatorname{aff}(P)\longrightarrow\mathbb R^d
\]
such that
\[
s(c)\in C_c,\qquad
\delta_C(c,s(c))\geq\kappa_c
\quad(c\in P\cap\mathbb Z^2).
\tag{5}
\]
If \(q>0\), then
\[
\inf_{\substack{
R\subseteq\operatorname{aff}(P)\text{ a proper closed halfspace}\\
z_0\in R}}
\sum_{c\in P\cap R\cap\mathbb Z^2}\delta_C(c,s(c))
\geq\frac W{64}.
\tag{6}
\]
If \(q=0\), then \(P=\{z_0\}\) and
\[
\delta_C(z_0,s(z_0))\geq\frac W{64}.
\tag{7}
\]
Consequently, taking \(E=\operatorname{vert}(P)\), condition (5) furnishes
one admissible pair in the registered anchored affine-certificate capacity
with value at least \(W/64\).

The use of the full autocorrelation, including its diagonal, is necessary
for (1).  More precisely, for every \(0<\varepsilon<1/64\) there is the
following finite abstract weight profile on \(\mathbb Z^2\).  Put
\[
u_+=(1,0),\qquad
u_1=(-1,4),\qquad
u_2=(-5,2),\qquad
u_3=(-1,-4),\qquad
\mathcal K=\{5,7,9,11\},
\]
and define
\[
w_0=\varepsilon,\qquad
w_{u_+}=\frac14-\varepsilon,\qquad
w_{ku_j}=\frac1{16}
\quad(k\in\mathcal K,\ 1\leq j\leq3),
\tag{8}
\]
with all other weights zero.  This profile has \(W=1\), satisfies
\[
w_z<\frac14\quad(z\in\mathbb Z^2),
\tag{9}
\]
\[
\sum_{z\in(a+L)\cap\mathbb Z^2}w_z<\frac12
\tag{10}
\]
for every coset of every primitive rank-one sublattice, has
\[
0\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{conv}\{z:w_z>0\},
\tag{11}
\]
and has marginal depth exactly \(1/4\) at \(0\).  Its ordered off-diagonal
same-parity mass is
\[
Q^\circ
:=
\sum_rW_r^2-\sum_z w_z^2
=\frac{57}{64}-\frac32\varepsilon
>\frac{16-e}{256}.
\tag{12}
\]
Nevertheless, if \(\xi\) denotes the unnormalized ordered off-diagonal
same-parity midpoint marginal,
\[
\xi_c:=
\sum_r
\sum_{\substack{
z,z'\equiv r\pmod2,\ z\neq z'\\
(z+z')/2=c}}
w_zw_{z'},
\tag{13}
\]
then the proper closed halfspace
\[
Q_+:=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2:x_1\geq0\}
\tag{14}
\]
contains \(0\) but satisfies
\[
\sum_{c\in Q_+\cap\mathbb Z^2}\xi_c=0.
\tag{15}
\]
For the full normalized autocorrelation profile in (1), the same halfspace
has
\[
\kappa(Q_+)
=
\frac14\left[
\varepsilon+
\frac{(1/4-\varepsilon)^2}{1-\varepsilon}
\right]
=
\frac1{64}+\frac{9\varepsilon}{64(1-\varepsilon)}.
\tag{16}
\]
Thus (1) is sharp as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), even under (9)--(12), while
the off-diagonal analogue is false.  The profile (8) is asserted only as an
abstract lattice-weight calibration; it is not asserted to be the fiber
profile of a convex body and therefore is not a counterexample to the
registered convex-body subgoal or to the locked target.
